I dropped 14 of the 20 hypotheses and kept 6. Most of the dropped ones had no clear mechanism and hedged both directions in their own rationale. Those were edit 1 avg_pool | edge 3 conv, edit 4 conv3x3 | edge 0 conv3x3, edit 5 conv3x3 | edge 1 conv1x1, edit 2 conv3x3 | edge 0 skip, edit 4 skip | edge 0 conv, edit 5 avg_pool | edge 1 conv, edit 2 conv1x1 | edge 5 conv, edit 0 conv1x1 | edge 4 pool, edit 3 skip | edge 4 conv, edit 1 conv3x3 | edge 0 conv1x1, edit 5 skip | edge 4 skip, edit 2 avg_pool | edge 4 conv, edit 1 skip | edge 5 pool and edit 5 conv1x1 | edge 2 skip.

The kept ones are the shortcut and redundancy cases, such as a direct skip or conv on edge 3 shrinking the gain from a conv elsewhere, and the pool on edge 4 with edge 3 removed.

The replacements rest on two mechanisms I expect to hold across all three datasets:
- **Replaced op:** swapping in a conv gains most when it replaces `none` or a parameter-free pool, and least when it replaces a skip.
- **Connectivity:** an edit on edge 4 or edge 2 does nothing when edge 0 is `none`, because node 1 is then unreachable.

I haven't tested any of these against benchmark data.
